acceptance: cleanBounded never returns invalid UTF-8 (test at the limit with a multi-byte rune)
A duplicate id resolves to the same item in the dep, connects and routing paths (test)
A malformed console-routed item emits a coded WARN at the plan-time gate (test)
fix: Truncate on a rune boundary, with a test using a multi-byte character at the limit. Resolve duplicate ids once, in one shared index, with a test. Run fileAreaRule and IsOperatorState on the same tokenized, locator-stripped entries that routing uses. Surface LoadDir warnings from RoutedResolver as a coded WARN.
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: Correctness nits in the queue reader with no observed failure.

summary: Found by comment-reduction batch 9 (2026-09-26) and reported without changing code. (1) cleanBounded truncates with mapped[:max] at a byte offset, so it can cut a multi-byte UTF-8 character in half and put invalid UTF-8 into prompt fields. (2) indexByID, used by the dep and connects rules, keeps the LAST item for a duplicate id, while RoutedResolver keeps the FIRST: two resolutions of one queue. (3) fileAreaRule and IsOperatorState read raw Files entries, while routing tokenizes entries and strips locators, so '(see go/internal/x/a.go)' gets the area '(see go/internal'. (4) RoutedResolver discards LoadDir's warnings, so a console-routed item with malformed JSON resolves as dispatchable at the plan-time gate. Failing open is deliberate, but here it is silent.
title: inboxbatch: cleanBounded can split a UTF-8 character into prompt fields, duplicate ids resolve differently in two places, and a malformed console-routed item silently resolves as dispatchable
